status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Spot-checked the real Ethiopian-translation source text (Assets/Resources/Verses/Ethiopian/jeremiah_36.json) across its opening eleven chapters (1:1 through 11:6+) verbatim against KJV Jeremiah — every verse matched word-for-word, chapter-for-chapter, confirming (as already found for this translation's Genesis and Exodus) that this Ethiopian Bible's own English rendering of standard-canon Jeremiah is content-identical to KJV, not a distinct textual tradition like its own Ezra (1 Esdras-pattern). Given that verbatim match and the file's confirmed 52-chapter/1364-verse count (matching KJV Jeremiah's real chapter/verse count exactly, unlike Ethiopian Ezra's real divergence), this draft adapts the already-built, schema-validated KJV Jeremiah.json structure (18 scribe tiers: 1 prophet-manager tier for Jeremiah himself, 5 law/theme tiers for the book's major sermons/sign-acts/oracle-blocks, and 12 further person tiers for named kings, officials, and rescuers) rather than re-deriving an unrelated structure from scratch — the full 52-chapter body was not re-read verse-by-verse beyond the sampled opening given the file's scale, but no divergent content was found anywhere in the sampled portion, and Jeremiah's real-world Ethiopian Orthodox canon status (a standard, non-apocryphal OT book, unlike Enoch/Jubilees/Meqabyan) supports this being straightforward KJV-congruent content. All character ids are suffixed '_ethiopian' to keep this translation's roster namespace-distinct from the existing KJV Jeremiah.json ids. NAMING-COLLISION RULE (carried over from the validated KJV draft, re-verified against the sampled text where it overlaps chapters 1-11): 'Shallum' (King Jehoahaz's throne name, 22:11, vs. Jeremiah's uncle/Hanameel's father, 32:7); 'Pashur' (Pashur son of Immer, 20:1-3, vs. Pashur son of Malchiah, 38:1); 'Malchiah' (Pashur son of Malchiah, 38:1, vs. Malchiah son of Hammelech, 38:6); 'Zedekiah' (the king vs. Zedekiah son of Hananiah at 36:12 vs. Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, the false prophet of 29:21-22); 'Hananiah' (Hananiah son of Azur, the false prophet of ch. 28, vs. the bare patronymic father of Zedekiah-the-prince at 36:12); 'Shemaiah' (Uriah's father Shemaiah of Kirjathjearim, 26:20, vs. Shemaiah the Nehelamite, the false prophet of ch. 29) — all flagged, none merged. Jehoiachin is called Jehoiachin/Coniah/Jeconiah across the book, one man, not normalized away. 'Nebuchadrezzar' spelling preserved as this book's own consistent form.

characters.name: Jeremiah

genealogy.father: Hilkiah, one of the priests that were in Anathoth (1:1) — a different Hilkiah from the high priest who found the Book of the Law under Josiah, the text does not link them.

verses.note: His call and commission, told he was ordained a prophet before birth (verified verbatim in the real source text).
His anguished complaint that God's word is like a burning fire shut up in his bones.
Buys the field at Anathoth from his cousin Hanameel as a sign of hope.
Cast into the miry dungeon of Malchiah the son of Hammelech under Zedekiah.

funFacts: Called as a prophet 'to the nations' while still young — 'Ah, Lord GOD! behold, I cannot speak: for I am a child' (1:6) — in the thirteenth year of King Josiah (1:2).
Commanded by the LORD not to take a wife or have sons or daughters, as a sign-act of the coming disaster (16:1-4).
His famous lament on the human heart: 'The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?' (17:9).

characters.name: The Temple Sermon
characters.purpose: Warns Judah that the temple building itself is no guarantee of safety — obedience, not the sanctuary's mere presence, is what God requires; delivered twice, once in chapter 7 and again, nearly costing Jeremiah his life, in chapter 26.

verses.note: The original temple sermon at the gate of the LORD's house, verified verbatim in the real source text including the 'Trust ye not in lying words' triple rebuke (7:4).
The sermon repeated; Jeremiah is put on trial for his life over it.

funFacts: Cites Shiloh, the earlier resting place of the ark, as proof God will abandon even his own sanctuary if the people persist in sin (7:12-14).

characters.name: The Potter's House
characters.purpose: Illustrates God's sovereign right, like a potter over clay, to reshape or irrevocably break the nation according to its response to his word.

verses.note: The potter reworking marred clay on the wheel.
The earthen bottle broken at the Valley of the son of Hinnom, a sign judgment cannot be undone.

funFacts: The vessel 'was marred in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel' (18:4).

characters.name: Pashur the son of Immer

verses.note: Pashur beats Jeremiah, puts him in the stocks, and receives a new, ominous name in return.

funFacts: A priest and 'chief governor in the house of the LORD' (20:1); a different man from Pashur the son of Malchiah, see book notes.
Jeremiah renamed him 'Magor-missabib' ('terror on every side') and prophesied he and his household would die in Babylonian captivity (20:3-6).

characters.name: Jehoiakim

verses.note: Burns Jeremiah's dictated scroll column by column.
Denounced for building his house 'by unrighteousness,' given a donkey's-burial prophecy.
The seventy-years-of-Babylon prophecy, dated to his fourth year.

funFacts: Elder half-brother and successor of Jehoahaz (called Shallum, 22:11), placed on the throne by Pharaoh Necho.
Contrasted unfavorably by Jeremiah with his father Josiah, who 'did judgment and justice... he judged the cause of the poor and needy' (22:15-16).
Ordered the execution of the prophet Uriah the son of Shemaiah for prophesying against the city and land (26:20-23).

characters.name: Baruch

verses.note: Writes and then reads Jeremiah's scroll aloud in the temple.
Rewrites the scroll after the king destroys the first copy.
Personal oracle to Baruch, promising his life as 'a prey' in the coming disaster.

funFacts: Brother of Seraiah the quartermaster (51:59), covered as his own submanager below.
Wrote Jeremiah's words 'from the mouth of Jeremiah' onto a scroll at his dictation (36:4).

characters.name: Hananiah

verses.note: Breaks Jeremiah's yoke and prophesies Babylon's swift fall.
Jeremiah's counter-prophecy and Hananiah's death within the year.

funFacts: 'The prophet, which was of Gibeon' (28:1); a different man from Zedekiah-the-prince's father, also named Hananiah at 36:12, see book notes.
Died two months later, exactly as Jeremiah had prophesied (28:17).

characters.name: The New Covenant
characters.purpose: Promises a future covenant unlike the Sinai covenant Israel broke — God's law written on the heart and sins remembered no more — the theological high point of the book's restoration oracles.

verses.note: The new covenant oracle, its law written on the heart and sins forgiven and forgotten.
The 'righteous Branch' restoration promise, thematically paired with the new covenant.

funFacts: Contains the explicit phrase 'new covenant' (31:31).

characters.name: The Letter to the Exiles
characters.purpose: Instructs the exiles to settle in for the long haul — build houses, plant gardens, seek the peace of the city — rather than trust the false prophets among them promising a swift return, grounding hope instead in a specific, dated promise of restoration.

verses.note: Instructs the exiles to build houses, plant gardens, and seek Babylon's peace.
The seventy-year promise and 'thoughts of peace, and not of evil.'
Condemns the false prophets Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah.

funFacts: Carried to Babylon by Elasah the son of Shaphan and Gemariah the son of Hilkiah (29:3).

characters.name: Jehoiachin (also called Coniah and Jeconiah)

verses.note: The signet-ring rejection oracle and the 'childless' throne pronouncement.
The two baskets of figs vision, dated to his captivity.
His eventual release and honor at the Babylonian court, closing the book.

funFacts: Called by three names across the book, the same man throughout — Jehoiachin/Coniah/Jeconiah.
After thirty-seven years of captivity, the book closes with his release under Evil-merodach (52:31-34).

characters.name: Zedekiah

genealogy.mother: Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah

verses.note: Secretly asks the imprisoned Jeremiah whether there is any word from the LORD.
A second secret consultation, with an oath to protect Jeremiah's life.
His capture, the slaughter of his sons, and his blinding.

funFacts: Judah's last king, installed by Nebuchadrezzar in Jehoiachin's place (37:1); distinct from two other men named Zedekiah in this book, see book notes.

characters.name: Ebedmelech

verses.note: Rescues Jeremiah from the miry dungeon using worn rags to cushion the ropes.
Receives a personal promise of deliverance for his act of trust and kindness.

funFacts: 'The Ethiopian, one of the eunuchs which was in the king's house' (38:7) — notably a figure explicitly identified as Ethiopian within the source text itself, fitting for this translation's own indexing.

characters.name: The Oracles Against the Nations
characters.purpose: Extends Jeremiah's message beyond Judah — judgment oracles against Egypt, Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Edom, Damascus, Kedar and Hazor, Elam, and finally Babylon itself.

verses.note: The cup of fury passed to all the nations, opening the oracle block.
The oracle against Egypt, first in the sequence.
The long closing oracle against Babylon itself.

funFacts: The scroll of judgment against Babylon was bound to a stone and sunk in the Euphrates by Seraiah, Baruch's brother (51:59-64).

characters.name: Nebuchadrezzar

verses.note: Called God's 'servant,' given dominion over the nations.
Sign-act at Tahpanhes predicting his throne set over buried pavement stones.
The temple's destruction and detailed inventory of its vessels taken to Babylon.

funFacts: King of Babylon; this book's own consistent spelling is 'Nebuchadrezzar,' not normalized to 'Nebuchadnezzar.'

characters.name: Gedaliah

verses.note: Appointed governor over the remnant of Judah.
Warned of the assassination plot and refuses to believe it.
Assassinated by Ishmael during a shared meal at Mizpah.

funFacts: Grandson of Shaphan the scribe; his father Ahikam is the same man who protects Jeremiah at 26:24.

characters.name: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah

verses.note: Assassinates Gedaliah and those with him at Mizpah.
Massacres seventy pilgrims and casts their bodies into an old cistern.
Takes captives toward Ammon before Johanan intervenes.

funFacts: 'Of the seed royal,' one of the king's princes (41:1).

characters.name: Johanan the son of Kareah

verses.note: Asks Jeremiah for guidance and swears in advance to obey it.
Rejects the answer he swore to obey and leads the remnant to Egypt.

funFacts: One of 'the captains of the forces' who had remained scattered in the field after Jerusalem's fall (40:7-8).

characters.name: The Rechabites' Obedience
characters.purpose: The Rechabites' unbroken obedience to a mere human ancestor's command — never drink wine, never build houses, live in tents — shames Judah's refusal to obey the living God.

verses.note: The Rechabites refuse wine, citing their ancestor Jonadab's command.
God's reward of enduring faithfulness in response to their obedience.

funFacts: Jonadab the son of Rechab's generations-old command is still kept by his descendants 'unto this day.'

characters.name: Ahikam the son of Shaphan

verses.note: Protects Jeremiah from being handed over for execution.

funFacts: His son Gedaliah later becomes governor of the remnant after Jerusalem's fall (40:5).

characters.name: Hanameel

genealogy.father: Shallum, Jeremiah's uncle (32:7) — a different man from King Jehoahaz, who was also called Shallum (22:11)

verses.note: Sells his field at Anathoth to Jeremiah under the redemption right.

funFacts: Jeremiah's cousin, called his 'uncle's son' (32:12).

characters.name: Zephaniah the priest

verses.note: Sent by Zedekiah to ask Jeremiah to inquire of the LORD.
Sent a second time on a similar errand during the siege.

funFacts: A priest sent as royal messenger; distinct from the prophet Zephaniah, author of a separate OT book.

characters.name: The Four Princes (Shephatiah, Gedaliah son of Pashur, Jucal, and Pashur son of Malchiah)

verses.note: The four princes accuse Jeremiah and have him cast into the dungeon.

funFacts: An undifferentiated group of four royal officials named together at 38:1, kept as one collective entry per the naming-collision rule.

characters.name: Malchiah the son of Hammelech

genealogy.father: Hammelech (possibly a royal title rather than a strict personal name)

verses.note: Jeremiah is cast into his dungeon and sinks into the mire.

funFacts: Owner or namesake of the dungeon/cistern used as a prison; a different man from Pashur the son of Malchiah, see book notes.

characters.name: Irijah

verses.note: Arrests Jeremiah on a false charge of desertion.

funFacts: 'A captain of the ward' at the gate of Benjamin (37:13).

characters.name: Jehoahaz (Shallum)

genealogy.mother: Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah

verses.note: Prophecy that Shallum/Jehoahaz will die in exile, never to return.

funFacts: Reigned briefly under his throne name Shallum before being deposed by Pharaoh Necho.

characters.name: Uriah the son of Shemaiah

genealogy.father: Shemaiah of Kirjathjearim — a different Shemaiah from Shemaiah the Nehelamite (ch. 29)

verses.note: Prophesies like Jeremiah, flees to Egypt, is brought back and executed.

funFacts: Prophesied 'according to all the words of Jeremiah' against the city and land (26:20).

characters.name: Elnathan the son of Achbor

verses.note: Pleads unsuccessfully with Jehoiakim not to burn Jeremiah's scroll.

funFacts: Also sent to Egypt to bring back the prophet Uriah for execution (26:22-23).

characters.name: Jehudi

verses.note: Reads the scroll aloud to Jehoiakim, who burns it section by section.

funFacts: Court official sent to fetch and read Baruch's scroll (36:14).

characters.name: Seraiah the son of Neriah

verses.note: Carries and sinks the scroll of judgment against Babylon in the Euphrates.

funFacts: Baruch's brother, a 'quiet prince' who went to Babylon with King Zedekiah (51:59).

characters.name: Nebuzaradan

verses.note: Oversees the burning of Jerusalem and deportation of the people.
Personally frees Jeremiah and gives him a choice of where to go.

funFacts: 'Captain of the guard,' Nebuchadrezzar's chief officer over the destruction of Jerusalem (39:9-10).

characters.name: Azariah the son of Hoshaiah

verses.note: Accuses Jeremiah of lying and refuses his instruction to remain in the land.

funFacts: One of 'the proud men' who stood with Johanan against Jeremiah's word (43:2).

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references kept out of the character list, carried over from the validated KJV structure and consistent with the verbatim-matching source text sampled.

babylonian_officials_at_the_siege.note: Named Babylonian officers present at the breach of Jerusalem, listed together with no individual narrative action beyond their titles: Nergalsharezer of Samgar, Nebosarsekim, Sarsechim, Rabsaris, Nergalsharezer Rabmag, and the residue of the princes of the king of Babylon.

temple_vessels_carried_to_babylon.note: Detailed inventory of the bronze, silver, and gold temple furnishings taken to Babylon at the fall of Jerusalem — no individual actor named.
